description: The version combination the OurFairy v1 backend is built and tested against. External dependencies (dsh, rikkahub) are pinned to exact product commits; the product repository itself locks its integration branch, because pinning a repository to its own branch tip would be self-referential and would fail after every merge. `researchUpstreamSha` is the upstream commit the readiness research was written against and is NEVER a product deliverable. A ticket worktree obtains the same combination by branching from each repo's `integrationBranch` tip and running scripts/combo.mjs verify.

ourfairy.note: Self repository: verify asserts the current worktree HEAD is the integration branch tip or an ancestor of it (the worktree is based on this combination), instead of comparing against a fixed commit. Product modules live under backend/, product launchers under scripts/.

dsh.note: productCommit is the fork's integration branch tip and has now advanced past researchUpstreamSha: ticket #26 landed the admission generalization (a registered second credential admitted as its own principal Peer, with the browser cookie path unchanged), and ticket #25 landed durable session ownership plus first-class delivery of a peer Session's message -- the owner is an optional compatible header extension (no SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION bump, v4 owns its own header codec, the released v2 contract untouched) and delivery is a new surface event type carrying no fabricated turn/step/stream. Widening AssistantMessage.source to accept a delivered (non-model) source reached further than the first consumer list (four production consumers and four existing tests needed narrowing), which is why the merge was held until typecheck was clean on both the host and client projects; the pushed pre-push hook re-ran typecheck on the merged commit and it passed. researchUpstreamSha stays fixed at the upstream commit the readiness research was written against and is never a product deliverable. build:lib:host builds the CLI/host libraries, but it is NOT sufficient: packages/client/tsdown.client.ts:120 returns SKIP_WORKSPACE_BUILD in the host pass for every package declared through clientBundle() without hostPhase, so a package such as @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection has no lib/index.js after build:lib:host while its package.json main points exactly there. build:lib:client is the DSH_BUILD_FACE=client pass that emits those Node loader entries and browser artifacts. Measured: without it, a profile mounting the `connection` row fails to import ('1 required plugin did not activate', ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on packages/client/connection/lib/index.js) in a checkout that had only ever run build:lib:host. build:native-system builds native/system/packages/linux-x64/bin/glibc/system.node, which the durable JSONL session writer requires (verified: without it a session flush fails to load the flock addon).

rikkahub.note: productCommit is the fork integration tip after T5/T6 remote chat/recovery and T9 attachments. Attachments use authenticated remote propose/chunk/complete, persist ordered upload IDs with the existing unknown-send request identity, expose original-byte downloads by session/message/index, and discard delayed work across account/session switches. Existing Markdown rendering and native session history remain in use. Owner relevant JVM suite passed 98/98 and debug APKs built; merger verifies source-tree equality and APK hashes and runs bounded attachment regressions. No phone/emulator, actual Android preference-disk fault, APK-to-real-backend, official-cloud image, signed-release or performance acceptance was run. researchUpstreamSha remains the research baseline. T16 adds authenticated speech transcription with existing remote chat input ownership and Android recording adapters. Existing local typing, camera and speech state arbitrate one input owner; delayed transcription is discarded after identity/session changes. JVM speech API/input tests and debug compilation passed with platform/provider substitutes; no real SiliconFlow account, microphone or device acceptance is claimed. T19 reuses the original Fairy visuals and local presentation preferences while presenting the latest remote snapshot, resolving terminal Markdown and preserving reading anchors. Presentation plus speech JVM regressions and release compilation passed after T16 integration. A test-signed release APK and offline measurement entry are available; actual device frame, memory and visual continuity measurements remain T22. Stage review fixes reading continuity by retaining the already-visible raw layout during settlement until the user returns to the tail or leaves that row, using native attempt/sequence association. Full Android 515-test suite and release packaging passed; device layout acceptance remains unclaimed. #61 states the attempt row key convention once: a single internal attemptRowKey(generation, attemptId) in RemotePresentation is shared by the settled-row key in RemoteChatPanel and the pair-to-key join in RemoteTranscript, and RemoteReadingTransitionTest now derives every key through it plus pins the literal format, so a format drift fails a test instead of silently disabling deferred terminal formatting. Merger verified merged source tree equals the implementer-accepted FINAL_SHA tree (identical tree sha) and re-ran the directed RemoteReadingTransitionTest (6 tests, 0 failures); full JVM 516-test suite and debug APKs are the implementer's evidence on that same tree. Merging the deferred onBeforeFormat/onRichPresented callback pair was intentionally left out of scope. #55 answers snapshot trust once: RemoteChatSnapshot.activityEstablishedAt(committedThrough) is the single rule (projection cursor and reported throughSeq both covered by the watermark, else status = 0), the activity getter only layers binding (connected && initialized) on top of it, and the sync loop decides notification settlement from that derived value instead of re-reading the unguarded latest.activity with its own predicate; the !syncing term is gone from the getter so there is one rule, not two. Merger verified the merged tree sha equals the implementer-accepted FINAL_SHA tree and re-ran the directed RemoteActivityTrustTest/StateTest/NotificationStateTest/NotificationWireTest (4 suites, 20 tests, 0 failures); the full 520-test JVM suite and assembleDebug are the implementer's evidence on that same tree. The acknowledged-based notification fact window, deliberately more conservative than the panel getter, was left unchanged. #59 decides RemoteChatBackend.read once: it is kept, with docs, because it is the client mirror of the documented /chat/read contract and the one-shot adapter on the same projection seam observe uses -- no page opens a session with it (observe's opening snapshot already carries everything a read returns), and deleting it would move no complexity while dropping the RemoteChatApiTest coverage that pins POST /chat/read. Only 22 lines of KDoc were added, no behaviour changed; merger verified the merged tree sha equals the implementer-accepted FINAL_SHA tree and re-ran the directed RemoteChatApiTest (18 tests, 0 failures), with the full 520-test JVM suite and assembleDebug as the implementer's evidence on that same tree. #60 states the foreground fact once: RemoteReceiveController no longer caches the app's foreground state, so a decision taken between lifecycle callbacks now asks the platform object (`platform.isForeground()`) instead of a remembered copy that could disagree with the publication path reading the same fact; the new read-side seam `RemoteReceivePlatform` is what both reception and publication ask, `RemoteNotificationPlatform` is left alone because merging it would put publish on a controller that only reads, and the service start/stop moved behind `RemoteReceiveServiceHost` solely so the controller can be driven from a JVM test without a Context. Merger verified the merged tree sha equals the implementer-accepted FINAL_SHA tree (fee6651e, `git diff --quiet` exit 0) and re-ran the directed RemoteReceiveControllerTest (4 tests, 0 failures); the full 71-suite / 524-test JVM run and assembleDebug are the implementer's evidence on that same tree. `RemoteReceiveService` and AndroidRemoteNotifications' own isForeground() remain untested (no Robolectric in this repo); no device/emulator, Firebase runtime or real-cloud acceptance is claimed. #56 answers cross-session notification backlog ownership: each RemoteChatState records the episode it owes in the ChatSyncRecord it already owns (notificationOwed, committed with the watermark) and no longer publishes or holds a platform, while RemoteReceiveState now drains every observed session's owed episodes into one reminder (publishBacklog) once no session is still catching up, preferring the account primary chat so the merged reminder still lands where the user reads; RemoteNotificationPlatform stays a two-method interface. Merger verified the merged tree sha equals the implementer-accepted FINAL_SHA tree (3c0e7cad, git diff --quiet exit 0) and re-ran the directed RemoteNotification*/RemoteActivityTrustTest/RemoteReceiveStateTest (5 suites, 22 tests) plus service.RemoteReceiveControllerTest (4 tests), 26 tests 0 failures; the full 72-suite / 527-test JVM run and assembleDebug are the implementer's evidence on that same tree. Implementer-recorded out-of-scope finding: RemoteChatState's before/cut fields were reported as cross-session shared and overwriting each other when several sessions are bound; merger found before/cut are per-instance and reception builds one RemoteChatState per session, so the finding is recorded for a follow-up ticket to verify and was not changed here. #63 turns the client tests into tests of the ChatSyncStore interface instead of the substitute's private map: persistent state (notificationThrough/episodeId/owed, pending, recovery cursors) is now read through `store.load`, writes are seeded via the stand-in's `seed`/`forget`, and the 'commit before attempt' ordering assertion reads the record back through the interface at publish time instead of restating the rule inside the substitute. The per-seq coverage builder duplicated in RemoteNotificationStateTest/RemoteChatRecoveryTest/RemoteChatStateTest is replaced by one shared test helper `RemoteChatFixtures` (remoteEvent/eventCoverage/deliveryProjection) in the projection package, so the continuity rule is stated once; cross-class companion builders were repointed to it. Only tests changed (9 files, +122/-115, test count unchanged at 527); no production code or new production API. Implementer red evidence: with a lying substitute whose load returns the stale record captured at bind time, the old assertions stayed green while the new `store.load` assertion failed, proving the old assertions never crossed the interface; green after restoring real load semantics. The third suggestion (a production validated-projection entry) was evaluated and deliberately not done because only tests would consume it. Merger verified the merged tree sha equals the implementer-accepted FINAL_SHA tree (474fd544, git diff --quiet 531fcb15 6f6cf7ff exit 0) and re-ran the directed data.remote.* regression (20 suites, 136 tests, 0 failures); the full 72-suite / 527-test JVM run and assembleDebug are the implementer's evidence on that same tree. No device/emulator, Firebase runtime or real-cloud acceptance is claimed. #58 answers whose session list the receiver publishes: the duplicate RemoteReceiveState.mutableSessions copy is gone and `sessions` is the very StateFlow OwnedSessionState publishes (the selected item derives from the same snapshot), while `bindIdentity` is called synchronously inside AccountSession.publish() and wired in IdentityModule, so the previous account's list is retired in the same turn as the identity publication instead of one dispatch later; RemoteReceiveController's identity collector bind and openNotification re-bind are gone, and with them the page's own isBoundTo guard and empty-snapshot fallback. Merger verified the merged tree sha equals the implementer-accepted FINAL_SHA tree (51b3f1a0, `git diff --quiet 6af8c3c8 81f1b06b` exit 0) and re-ran the directed data.remote.* + service.* regression plus the two identity navigation suites (28 suites, 202 tests, 0 failures); the full 72-suite / 530-test JVM run and assembleDebug are the implementer's evidence on that same tree. Koin IdentityModule wiring and the page-guard deletion are compile-level/module-level only (the repo has no Koin or Compose JVM test infrastructure). No device/emulator, Firebase runtime or real-cloud acceptance is claimed. #68 removes the forwarding shell: RemoteReceiveState no longer restates OwnedSessionState's refresh/create/select/read/returnToPrimary or its sessions snapshot alias; it exposes the very `owned` instance that reception binds and watches, and IdentitySessionsPage drives that instance directly. The new RemoteReceiveStateTest asserts the page-driven state is the same instance reception binds (6 tests in that class). Merger verified the merged tree sha equals the implementer-accepted FINAL_SHA tree (0059a662, `git diff --quiet 5c8f903b c3eea8a0` exit 0) and re-ran the directed data.remote.* + ui.identity.* + service.RemoteReceiveControllerTest regression (27 suites, 169 tests, 0 failures); the full 72-suite / 531-test JVM run and assembleDebug are the implementer's evidence on that same tree. The ticket's named caller RemoteReceiveSetup does not hold RemoteReceiveState at all — the only caller of the five methods was IdentitySessionsPage — and the page/Koin wiring remains compile-level only (no Compose/Koin JVM test infrastructure); no device/emulator, Firebase runtime or real-cloud acceptance is claimed. Map #69 final review fixes: settleReminders renamed for the one reminder role, isCatchingUp holds the backlog while a session is still opening or catching up (a failed attempt stops holding), a claim that outlived its binding is retired instead of replayed, one RemoteForegroundPlatform declares isForeground for both boundaries, and the read/observe claim now states only what the client can prove.

backend.agentModelNote: Single source of truth for the model selection this combination runs. The bundle's agent-default-model row declares the same pair for entry layers (ticket #28 consumes it); the launcher passes this pair to the probe, which passes it explicitly as agentOptions because no entry layer is mounted in the v1 baseline. 'doctor' checks backend/v1-bundle/cordis.patch.yml against these values so the two declarations cannot drift apart.
